# ExcelCars PostgreSQL Target Schema
## Status: Current as of migration completion

**Database:** `excelcars` on Postgres 17 (`excelcars-db` container, part of this project's `docker-compose.yml`)
**Source:** SQL Server `ExcelCars` — itself a merge of the live production database (`ExcelCarsNew`) and its pre-2023 archived predecessor (`ExcelCarsBackup`), reunified before this migration so no historical data was left behind.
**ORM:** Prisma, schema at `prisma/schema.prisma`, generated by introspection against this database.

## 1. Summary stats

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Tables | 35 |
| Foreign keys | 88 |
| CHECK constraints | 16 |
| Primary keys | 35 (every table) |
| Total rows | 693,968 |

## 2. Migration method

1. Hardened the source schema in SQL Server first: added missing foreign keys (validated against live data for orphans before each one), added indexes alongside every FK, added `CHECK` constraints on clean status/classification columns, fixed wrong data types (`Price`, `Registration_No`), converted denormalized text columns (car make/model/variant, agent/bank contacts, customer contact info) into real foreign keys against proper master tables.
2. Migrated schema + data from SQL Server into this Postgres database using `pgloader`, with automatic `downcase identifiers` (works cleanly here since the source already used underscores as word separators, so lowercasing alone produces valid snake_case).
3. Fixed everything `pgloader` didn't handle automatically:
   - Moved all tables from the `dbo` schema it created into Postgres's standard `public` schema
   - Recreated all `CHECK` constraints (not migrated automatically) — caught one real data bug in the process: a `Followup_Inquiry` row had `"Followup"` instead of `"FollowUp"`, invisible under SQL Server's case-insensitive collation, a real constraint violation under Postgres's case-sensitive comparison
   - Recreated the filtered/partial unique index on `registration_no` with correct Postgres `WHERE`-clause syntax (`pgloader` silently dropped the filter and created a plain index instead)
   - Converted all 32 identity/PK columns from `bigint` (pgloader's default) back to `integer`, matching both the original SQL Server `int` type and the FK columns that already referenced them — the mismatch otherwise blocks Prisma Client generation even though Postgres itself accepts it
4. Generated `prisma/schema.prisma` via `prisma db pull`, then applied two naming passes:
   - `prisma-case-format` — PascalCase model names, camelCase field names, mapped back to the real snake_case table/column names via `@map`/`@@map`. The database itself stays pure snake_case; only the Prisma/TypeScript layer is camelCase.
   - A custom script (`scripts/rename-relations.js`) cleaning up Prisma's auto-generated disambiguation names for tables with multiple FKs to the same target (overwhelmingly the `created_by`/`updated_by` → `user_table` pattern present on almost every table) — e.g. `userTableRtoAgentCreatedByTouserTable` → `createdByUser`.
   - **Both passes must be re-run after any `prisma db pull --force`**, which wipes manual schema edits and reverts to raw introspected names.

## 3. New tables introduced during this migration

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `access_function_role` | Junction table replacing `Access_Function.Role_ID`, which was a comma-packed string (`',1,2,4,'`) — the single biggest structural fix in the original schema |
| `partner_master` | Consolidates agent/bank contact info that was previously duplicated as free text across `Insurance_Main`, `RTO_Agent`, `DSA_Management`, `Loan_Management` |

## 4. Text-to-FK conversions

Car make/model/variant text columns were converted to `fk_variant_id` (referencing `car_variant_master`) on `inventory_management`, `inquiry_car_details`, `insurance_main`, `rto_agent`, and `customer_feedback`. Unmatched text values where the Make and Model matched an existing catalog entry were auto-created as new catalog variants (44 new rows added to `car_variant_master` this way — genuine new trims, not typos, since Insurance/RTO/Feedback service customer-owned cars that were never dealership inventory). Unmatched values where the Make or Model itself didn't match anything were **not** auto-created, to avoid polluting the catalog with typo'd duplicates (see Section 6).

All original text columns were preserved, renamed with a `_legacy` suffix (e.g. `make_legacy`, `agent_name_legacy`) rather than dropped — kept as an audit trail, not read by any application code going forward.

## 5. Post-merge fixes (this pass)

- **`inventory_management.tax`** — confirmed this is a categorical field (`'Individual'` / `'Corporate'`, the owner's tax-registration type), not a numeric value. Added a `CHECK` constraint; no numeric cast, unlike `Price`.
- **Orphaned FK references resolved** — 33 rows in `inquiry_car_details` and 26 rows in `followup_inquiry` referenced `Inquiry` records deleted before any FK constraint ever existed to prevent it (dating back to ~2015, before the source system had any referential integrity). Nulled the dangling references rather than leaving them pointing at nonexistent rows or fabricating replacement parents, then added both FK constraints (previously blocked by these orphans).
- **`dsa_management`** upgraded from Model-only (`fk_model_id`) to full Make/Model/Variant (`fk_variant_id`), matching every sibling module (Insurance, Loan, RTO). Table had zero rows at the time, so this was a pure schema change with no data migration.
- **Passwords hashed.** `user_table.password` was plaintext (confirmed directly — e.g. `Admin99`, `SuperAdmin0909`, fully readable). Hashed in place with bcrypt via Postgres `pgcrypto` (`$2a$` format, compatible with any standard Node.js bcrypt library), column renamed to `password_hash`. Decision made explicitly: hash in place, no forced reset — existing credentials keep working, now stored safely.

## 6. Known open items — flagged, not silently resolved

**10 `customer_feedback` rows need manual review**, not automated fixing:

| feedback_id | car_make (as entered) | car_model | car_variant | issue |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | Mercedes | *(empty)* | *(empty)* | Make only, no model/variant — insufficient data to link at all |
| 20 | Benz E class | *(empty)* | *(empty)* | Make+model crammed into one field |
| 23 | merc | c class | *(empty)* | Make typo; no variant text to link even if make were fixed |
| 27 | MERCEDES | GL 350 | CDI | Model doesn't match catalog (`GL` exists, not `GL 350`) — reinterpreting the field boundary is a guess, not a fix |
| 34 | mercedez | E 200 | petrol | Same pattern — `E Class` exists, `E 200` doesn't |
| 43 | lange rover | sport hse | *(empty)* | Make typo (`Land Rover`); model+trim crammed together |
| 51 | BMW | X5 | *(empty)* | Model exists in catalog, but no variant text to link |
| 55 | bmw | 730ld | *(empty)* | Value looks like a variant, entered in the model field |
| 56 | TOYOTA FORTUNER | 2011 | *(empty)* | Make+model crammed together; "model" field actually contains a year |
| 57 | mercedes | c250 | avantgarde | Same field-boundary ambiguity as #27/#34 |

Seven of the ten have no variant text at all — `fk_variant_id` links at variant granularity, so no text correction can produce a link without one. The other three require guessing how the business intends to split garbled Make/Model/Variant text, which risks creating incorrect catalog entries. Left as `NULL`, with `*_legacy` text intact for whoever reviews these.

## 7. Naming convention reference

Database: `snake_case` throughout (tables and columns). Prisma/TypeScript: `PascalCase` models, `camelCase` fields — bridged via `@map`/`@@map`, transparent to the database. Relation field names favor readability over Prisma's default disambiguation scheme (see Section 2).
